title: The Case For More Mega-Cap Outperformance
gist: Gavekal argues mega-cap tech outperformance is not over despite October falls of 14-20% in Nvidia, Meta and Alphabet and a 6pp lag versus the equal-weighted S&P 500, driven by AI capex financing and return worries. The text is a teaser; the supporting reasons are not given.

insights.claim: Since early October 2026, Nvidia has fallen 14.5%, Meta 17.1% and Alphabet 20.4%.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Sharp drawdowns in AI leaders may offer entry points if the mega-cap outperformance thesis holds.

insights.claim: Investors have become nervous about how the AI capex boom is being financed and jittery about the returns big tech will earn on the trillions already invested.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: AI financing and ROI doubts are the market-stated driver of the selloff.
insights.quote: investors have grown nervous about how the AI capex boom is being financed

insights.claim: Since the end of September the cap-weighted S&P 500 has underperformed the equal-weighted S&P 500 by 6 percentage points.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The breadth rotation away from mega-caps has been sizeable in a month.

insights.claim: Mega-cap tech stocks have driven US market outperformance over the last 10 years, and the author argues there are solid reasons to think this era is not ending.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Author favors buying the mega-cap dip over rotating to equal-weight; reasons are paywalled.
insights.quote: So, is the era of mega-cap outperformance coming to its end? There are solid reasons to think not.
